title: A simplified perchloric acid workflow with neutralization (PCA-N) for democratizing deep plasma proteomics at population scale - Submission04
projectDescription: This project presents PCA-N, a novel plasma proteomics workflow that uses perchloric acid with neutralization to dramatically improve sample preparation efficiency. By eliminating solid-phase extraction and enabling 384-well plate compatibility, PCA-N reduces sample volume requirements to just 5 μL, cuts costs to under $1 per sample, and allows processing of up to 13,000 samples daily. Validated on over 34,000 samples across 311 days, this method doubles proteome depth compared to conventional approaches while maintaining robust measurement precision, making large-scale plasma proteomics studies feasible for biomarker discovery and precision medicine.
sampleProcessingProtocol: The PCA-N workflow consists of several key steps:  1. Dilute 5 μL plasma with 25 μL water and mix with 25 μL perchloric acid (1 M, final concentration 0.5 M)  2. Incubate at 4°C for 60 minutes in 96-well plates  3. Centrifuge at 4000 x g for 20 minutes at 4°C  4. Transfer supernatant (24 μL) to 384-well plate  5. Neutralize with sodium hydroxide solution (1.4 M, 8 μL) to pH 8-8.5  6. Add reduction/alkylation/denaturation reagents (DTT, CAA, TEAB buffer)  7. Heat at 95°C for 10 minutes  8. Add Trypsin/LysC for overnight digestion  9. Stop digestion with TFA  10. Load onto Evotips for LC-MS/MS analysis
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw mass spectrometry data was analyzed using the following steps:  1. Raw files were processed using DIA-NN 1.8.1 on a high-performance computing cluster  2. An in silico predicted library approach was employed without requiring experimental spectral libraries  3. Mass accuracy and MS1 accuracy were set to 10 ppm with a scan window radius of 6  4. Missing values were imputed using K-nearest neighbors (KNN) algorithm with a minimum valid value threshold of 5% across samples  5. Protein quantification employed a multi-layered coefficient of variation (CV) approach to assess analytical, technical, and biological variability  6. Depletion/enrichment analysis was performed by calculating delta values (Δ) between PCAᴺ and NEAT preparations to classify proteins as enriched (Δ>0) or depleted (Δ<0)  7. Rank stability analysis was implemented to evaluate consistency of measurement precision across experimental conditions  8. Dimensionality reduction using t-SNE with correlation distance metrics was applied to visualize complex relationships in the proteomic data Temporal stability was assessed through hierarchical clustering and moving average trend analysis with a 10-day window
